1CO.P.2.1-5.text: Paul’s Message by the Spirit’s Power

1CO.P.6.18-20.text: The Temple of the Holy Spirit

1CO.P.15.50-58.text: Where, O Death, Is Your Victory?

1CO.1.4-6.text: Paul thanks God for the grace given to the Corinthians

1CO.1.7-9.text: God is faithful and will keep believers to the end

1CO.1.10-11.text: Paul urges the church to agree, because of quarrels

1CO.1.12-13.text: The Corinthians divide by following different leaders

1CO.1.14-16.text: Paul baptized only a few of the Corinthians

1CO.1.17-17.text: Christ sent Paul to preach the gospel, not to baptize

1CO.1.18-19.text: The cross seems foolish to some but is God’s power

1CO.1.20-21.text: God made the world’s wisdom foolish and saves believers

1CO.1.22-23.text: Paul preaches Christ crucified to Jews and Greeks

1CO.1.24-25.text: Christ is God’s power and wisdom for those called

1CO.1.26-27.text: God chose weak and foolish people to shame the strong

1CO.1.28-29.text: God chose lowly people so that no one can boast

1CO.1.30-31.text: Christ is wisdom from God; believers boast in the Lord

1CO.2.1-2.text: Paul came to Corinth preaching only Christ crucified

1CO.2.3-5.text: Paul came in weakness so faith would rest on God’s power

1CO.2.6-7.text: Paul speaks God’s hidden wisdom to the mature

1CO.2.8-9.text: Rulers did not understand and crucified the Lord of glory

1CO.2.10-11.text: God reveals his wisdom to believers by the Spirit

1CO.2.12-13.text: Paul speaks words taught by the Spirit, not by men

1CO.2.14-16.text: People without the Spirit cannot understand God’s things

1CO.3.1-2.text: Paul calls the Corinthians infants who need milk

1CO.3.3-5.text: Jealousy shows the Corinthians are still worldly

1CO.3.6-7.text: Paul planted, Apollos watered, but God made it grow

1CO.3.8-9.text: Paul and Apollos work together for God and are rewarded

1CO.3.10-11.text: Jesus Christ is the foundation; builders must be careful

1CO.3.12-13.text: Fire will test the quality of each builder’s work

1CO.3.14-15.text: Builders whose work survives will receive a reward

1CO.3.16-17.text: The Corinthians are God’s holy temple

1CO.3.18-20.text: Worldly wisdom is foolishness to God

1CO.3.21-23.text: Paul tells believers to stop boasting in men

1CO.4.1-2.text: Paul says God’s stewards must be found faithful

1CO.4.3-4.text: Paul says the Lord, not people, is his judge

1CO.4.5-5.text: Believers should not judge before the Lord comes

1CO.4.6-7.text: Paul tells the Corinthians not to be proud of one man

1CO.4.8-9.text: Paul says apostles are like prisoners facing death

1CO.4.10-11.text: Paul contrasts weak, hungry apostles with wise Corinthians

1CO.4.12-13.text: Paul says apostles bless and endure when mistreated

1CO.4.14-16.text: Paul is the Corinthians’ father and asks for imitation

1CO.4.17-18.text: Paul sends Timothy to remind the Corinthians of his ways

1CO.4.19-21.text: Paul will come soon and test the proud people’s power

1CO.5.1-2.text: Paul rebukes the church for allowing a man’s immorality

1CO.5.3-5.text: Paul says the church must hand the man over to Satan

1CO.5.6-8.text: Paul says a little sin spreads, so believers must be pure

1CO.5.9-10.text: Believers need not avoid all sinful people in the world

1CO.5.11-13.text: Believers must not eat with a brother who lives in sin

1CO.6.1-3.text: Paul asks why believers go to court before unbelievers

1CO.6.4-6.text: Paul says believers should settle disputes in the church

1CO.6.7-8.text: Paul says it is better to be wronged than to wrong others

1CO.6.9-11.text: Paul says the wicked will not inherit God’s kingdom

1CO.6.12-13.text: Paul says the body is for the Lord, not immorality

1CO.6.14-15.text: Paul says believers’ bodies are members of Christ

1CO.6.16-17.text: Paul says believers are one with the Lord in spirit

1CO.6.18-18.text: Paul urges believers to flee from sexual immorality

1CO.6.19-20.text: Believers’ bodies belong to God and are his temple

1CO.7.1-2.text: Because of immorality, each person should have a spouse

1CO.7.3-4.text: Husbands and wives belong to each other in marriage

1CO.7.5-7.text: Paul tells married believers not to deprive each other

1CO.7.8-9.text: Unmarried people and widows may stay single or marry

1CO.7.10-11.text: The Lord commands wives and husbands not to divorce

1CO.7.12-14.text: Paul says believers should stay with unbelieving spouses

1CO.7.15-16.text: If an unbeliever leaves, the believer is not bound

1CO.7.17-19.text: Circumcision is nothing; keeping God’s commands counts

1CO.7.20-24.text: Believers should stay in the situation of God’s call

1CO.7.25-26.text: Paul gives advice about virgins in a time of crisis

1CO.7.27-28.text: Paul says marrying is not sin but brings troubles

1CO.7.29-31.text: Paul warns believers that this world is passing away

1CO.7.32-34.text: Unmarried believers can serve the Lord with less concern

1CO.7.35-35.text: Paul wants believers to be devoted to the Lord

1CO.7.36-38.text: A man may marry his betrothed, but not marrying is better

1CO.7.39-40.text: A widow may marry a believer but is happier alone

1CO.8.1-3.text: Knowledge makes people proud, but love builds up

1CO.8.4-6.text: Paul says an idol is nothing; there is one God

1CO.8.7-7.text: Some believers have a weak conscience about idol food

1CO.8.8-10.text: Knowing believers must not make the weak stumble

1CO.8.11-13.text: Paul will not eat meat if it causes a brother to stumble

1CO.9.1-2.text: Paul says the Corinthians prove he is an apostle

1CO.9.3-6.text: Paul defends his right to food and drink

1CO.9.7-8.text: Paul uses soldiers, farmers and shepherds as examples

1CO.9.9-11.text: The Law says workers should share in the harvest

1CO.9.12-14.text: Paul gave up his right to support for the gospel

1CO.9.15-16.text: Paul is obligated to preach the gospel

1CO.9.17-18.text: Paul’s reward is to preach the gospel free of charge

1CO.9.19-20.text: Paul makes himself a slave to everyone to win people

1CO.9.21-23.text: Paul becomes all things to all people for the gospel

1CO.10.1-4.text: Israel’s fathers all had the same spiritual food and drink

1CO.10.5-6.text: God was not pleased with most of the Israelites

1CO.10.7-8.text: Paul warns believers against idols and sexual sin

1CO.10.9-10.text: Paul warns believers not to test Christ or complain

1CO.10.11-13.text: God provides a way out of temptation for believers

1CO.10.14-17.text: The cup and the one loaf join believers as one body

1CO.10.18-19.text: Israel shared in the altar by eating sacrifices

1CO.10.20-22.text: Believers cannot share the Lord’s table and demons’ table

1CO.10.23-24.text: Paul says believers should seek the good of others

1CO.10.25-27.text: Believers may eat any meat without asking questions

1CO.10.28-30.text: Believers should not eat food said to be offered to idols

1CO.10.31-33.text: Believers do everything for God’s glory and others’ good

1CO.11.1-4.text: Paul praises believers and explains who is head

1CO.11.5-6.text: A woman who prays with head uncovered dishonors her head

1CO.11.7-8.text: Paul says man is God’s image and woman came from man

1CO.11.9-10.text: A woman should have a sign of authority on her head

1CO.11.11-12.text: In the Lord, man and woman need each other

1CO.11.13-16.text: Paul says nature and church custom support head covering

1CO.11.17-19.text: Paul criticizes the Corinthians for divisions in gatherings

1CO.11.20-22.text: Paul rebukes believers who eat without sharing

1CO.11.23-24.text: Jesus breaks the bread and says it is his body

1CO.11.25-26.text: Jesus gives the cup, and believers proclaim his death

1CO.11.27-30.text: Believers must examine themselves before the Lord’s Supper

1CO.11.31-32.text: The Lord’s discipline keeps believers from condemnation

1CO.11.33-34.text: Paul tells believers to wait for one another to eat

1CO.12.1-3.text: Only the Holy Spirit lets believers say Jesus is Lord

1CO.12.4-6.text: There are different gifts, but one Spirit, Lord and God

1CO.12.7-8.text: The Spirit gives each believer a gift for the common good

1CO.12.9-11.text: The one Spirit gives faith, healing, miracles and more

1CO.12.12-13.text: Believers are many parts but one body in Christ

1CO.12.14-17.text: The body needs many parts, not only one

1CO.12.18-20.text: God arranged the parts of the body as he planned

1CO.12.21-24.text: The weaker parts of the body are needed and honored

1CO.12.25-26.text: Believers care for one another in suffering and honor

1CO.12.27-27.text: Paul says the Corinthians are the body of Christ

1CO.12.28-29.text: God gives the church apostles, prophets and teachers

1CO.12.30-31.text: Not all have the same gift; Paul shows the best way

1CO.13.1-3.text: Paul says gifts are worth nothing without love

1CO.13.4-7.text: Paul describes what love is like

1CO.13.8-10.text: Love never fails, but prophecy and knowledge will end

1CO.13.11-13.text: Faith, hope and love remain, and love is greatest

1CO.14.1-4.text: Paul urges believers to seek love and prophecy

1CO.14.5-6.text: Paul wants believers to prophesy so the church is built up

1CO.14.7-9.text: Musical instruments show that clear words are needed

1CO.14.10-11.text: Paul says unknown languages make people strangers

1CO.14.12-14.text: Paul urges the Corinthians to build up the church

1CO.14.15-16.text: Paul will pray and sing with spirit and with mind

1CO.14.17-19.text: Paul prefers five clear words to ten thousand in a tongue

1CO.14.20-21.text: Paul tells believers to think like adults, not children

1CO.14.22-23.text: Tongues are a sign for unbelievers, prophecy for believers

1CO.14.24-25.text: Prophecy leads an unbeliever to worship God

1CO.14.26-28.text: Paul gives rules for speaking in tongues in church

1CO.14.29-30.text: Two or three prophets speak and others weigh the words

1CO.14.31-33.text: Prophets take turns because God is a God of peace

1CO.14.34-36.text: Paul tells women to be silent in the churches

1CO.14.37-38.text: Paul says his words are the Lord’s command

1CO.14.39-40.text: Paul urges believers to prophesy and keep good order

1CO.15.1-2.text: Paul reminds the Corinthians of the gospel he preached

1CO.15.3-4.text: Christ died for sins, was buried and was raised

1CO.15.5-7.text: Paul lists people who saw the risen Christ

1CO.15.8-9.text: Christ appeared to Paul, the least of the apostles

1CO.15.10-11.text: Paul says God’s grace made him what he is

1CO.15.12-14.text: Paul says no resurrection means Christ is not raised

1CO.15.15-17.text: Paul says if Christ is not raised, faith is useless

1CO.15.18-19.text: Without the resurrection, believers are most to be pitied

1CO.15.20-21.text: Christ has been raised as the firstfruits of the dead

1CO.15.22-23.text: In Christ all will be made alive, each in his own turn

1CO.15.24-26.text: Christ will destroy every enemy, and death is the last

1CO.15.27-28.text: God puts all under Christ, and the Son submits to God

1CO.15.29-30.text: Paul asks why people are baptized for the dead

1CO.15.31-32.text: Paul faces death daily and asks what he would gain

1CO.15.33-34.text: Paul warns the Corinthians against bad company and sin

1CO.15.35-36.text: Paul answers how the dead are raised and with what body

1CO.15.37-39.text: God gives each seed its own body, and bodies differ

1CO.15.40-41.text: Heavenly bodies and earthly bodies have different splendor

1CO.15.42-44.text: The dead are raised in glory with a spiritual body

1CO.15.45-46.text: Paul compares the first Adam with Christ, the last Adam

1CO.15.47-49.text: Believers will bear the likeness of the heavenly man

1CO.15.50-51.text: Paul tells a mystery: believers will all be changed

1CO.15.52-53.text: At the last trumpet the dead rise and believers are changed

1CO.15.54-55.text: Paul says death will be swallowed up in victory

1CO.15.56-57.text: Paul thanks God for victory through Jesus Christ

1CO.15.58-58.text: Paul urges believers to stay firm in the Lord’s work

1CO.16.1-2.text: Paul tells the Corinthians to set aside money each week

1CO.16.3-4.text: Paul will send chosen men with the gift to Jerusalem

1CO.16.5-6.text: Paul plans to visit the Corinthians after Macedonia

1CO.16.7-9.text: Paul will stay in Ephesus because of great work there

1CO.16.13-14.text: Paul urges believers to be alert, strong, and loving

1CO.16.15-16.text: Paul asks believers to follow Stephanas and other workers

1CO.16.17-18.text: Paul is glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus came

1CO.16.19-20.text: Churches and friends send greetings to the Corinthians

1CO.16.21-24.text: Paul closes with his own greeting and love for believers
